dossier.public_summary: The dip alternates between about twice as deep and very shallow from transit to transit, with an odd-even difference of 4.9 sigma and a second dip at 6.98 sigma. Depths change dramatically within the same instrument, including near-zero and near-zero-negative events driven by three deep outliers. This pattern matches a pair of unequal stellar eclipses folded at half their true 25-day period, not a stable planet transit.

reasons.why: Odd and even depths differ strongly (depth_odd_ppm 1181 vs depth_even_ppm 497.5, depth_difference 0.5789) with diff_sigma 4.923, expected share 0.4433 at refit.snr 25.1; also at least 3 transits used per fit. This is the primary signature of an eclipsing binary folded at twice its period (period_x2 25.2 d) or a blend with alternating primary/secondary eclipses.

A second dip well above noise criteria coincides with the odd/even mismatch. Depth ~25% of the primary and phase offset ~0.05393 argue for a binarity/second eclipse, not a planetary secondary; phase_curve ratio_to_depth 0.05174 chi2 5.869 does not dominate but is consistent with ellipsoidal/spot modulation on a binary.
reasons.value: 6.984 at phase 0.4461, depth_ppm 246.2, depth_over_dip 0.2477 vs best_brightening_snr 5.84

reasons.why: Depth is not steady and is driven by a few bad transits (share_of_top_3 0.957, outliers 2142 ppm sigma 7.3 and 2024 ppm sigma 7.0 vs -55 ppm sigma -5.7). sector_depths_by_source verdict changes_within_a_source with p_constant_all 2.1476928709572834e-37 (SPOC 2-min p_constant 3.480277924693265e-10, TESS-SPOC p_constant 0.0011108254080741049) shows intrinsic eclipse-depth changes expected for unequal primary/secondary eclipses, not a planet with steady transits.
reasons.value: transit_depths p_consistent 1.6486470149818104e-33, chi2 170.86611386455027 dof 7; sectors p_constant 2.854e-37

reasons.why: No neighbour within one TESS pixel can plausibly cause the 980.8 ppm dip (closest that_could sep_arcsec 82.3 delta_mag 4.42 eclipse_needed 0.0576) and difference imaging cannot off-set the target. With flat-bottom shape not V-shaped (shape.v_sigma 1.683) and duration.ratio 0.9864, rv, remains planet-sized (rp_rearth 2.703) but flat shapes can also be stellar; the positive combined binary signatures odd/even + secondary + inconsistent depths provide positive evidence for a binary/dip on the target folded at half period rather than a planet.
